title: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecule
topicTitle: Average translational kinetic energy of gas molecule
summary: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecule covers essential principles and applications.
specificConditions: **Equipartition Result:** The average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\langle KE_{trans} angle =  rac{3}{2} k_B T =  rac{3}{2}  rac{R}{N_A} T$. This comes from 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing $ rac{1}{2} k_B T$ via equipartition.

**Temperature Proportionality:** $\langle KE_{trans} angle \propto T$ — absolute temperature is a direct measure of average translational kinetic energy. This is why Kelvin scale is fundamental: at $T=0$, translational KE is zero (classically).

**Internal Energy of Monatomic Gas:** For a monatomic ideal gas, $U = N \langle KE_{trans} angle =  rac{3}{2} nRT$. The internal energy is purely translational KE. For diatomic/polyatomic gases, $U$ includes rotational and vibrational contributions as well.
